subject: ela
intro: Revising and editing make your writing stronger. Revising means looking at the big picture: Does every sentence stay on topic? Are your ideas clear? Can you add details or examples to make your writing better? Editing means fixing smaller errors: spelling, punctuation, and capitalization. Good writers ask themselves: 'Is any sentence off-topic? Can I make a sentence more detailed or interesting? Does my piece have a clear beginning and ending?' With guidance from your teacher or a classmate, you can make your writing go from good to great.

items.prompt:
Read this paragraph. Identify the sentence that is off-topic and should be removed.

'Dogs make wonderful pets. They are loyal and love spending time with their owners. My uncle has a pet iguana. Dogs can be trained to do amazing things, like guide people who are blind or help during emergencies.'

steps: Read each sentence and ask: does it relate to the main idea (dogs as wonderful pets)?
Sentence 1: about dogs. On-topic.
Sentence 2: about dogs' loyalty. On-topic.
Sentence 3: 'My uncle has a pet iguana.' This is about an iguana, not dogs. OFF-TOPIC.
Sentence 4: about dogs' training abilities. On-topic.
The off-topic sentence is 'My uncle has a pet iguana.'
solution.answer: The off-topic sentence is 'My uncle has a pet iguana.' It does not relate to dogs.

items.prompt:
Read this weak sentence. Revise it by adding at least two specific details.

Weak: 'We had a good time at the beach.'

steps: Ask: WHO was there? WHAT did they do? WHAT did it look, sound, or feel like?
Add details about what made it good: activities, feelings, senses.
Revised: 'We had an amazing time at the beach, building a giant sandcastle with four towers and swimming in the cool, salty waves until our fingers turned wrinkly.'
solution.answer: Revised: 'We had an amazing time at the beach, building a giant sandcastle with four towers and swimming in the cool, salty waves until our fingers turned wrinkly.'

items.prompt:
Read this paragraph. Which detail could be added to make it stronger? Choose the best option.

'I love going to the library. There are so many books to choose from. I always leave with a big stack to read at home.'

A) 'My teacher's name is Mrs. Park.'
B) 'Last week, I discovered a whole shelf of adventure stories about kids exploring jungles and solving mysteries, and I checked out four of them.'
C) 'Libraries have been around for a long time.'

steps: Ask: which option adds a specific detail that supports the main idea (loving the library and its books)?
Option A is about the teacher — off-topic.
Option C is a general fact about libraries but does not make the personal experience more vivid.
Option B gives a specific example of what the writer found and checked out — this directly strengthens the paragraph by showing a real experience.
solution.answer: B — it adds a specific, vivid detail that supports the main idea.

items.prompt:
Read this student paragraph. Identify ONE problem with focus and explain how to fix it.

'Our class went on a field trip to the science museum. We saw a movie about space in the dome theater. I have a cat named Whiskers who likes to sleep on my bed. We also got to touch real fossils and look at them through magnifying glasses.'

steps: The paragraph is about a field trip to the science museum.
Read each sentence to check if it belongs.
'I have a cat named Whiskers who likes to sleep on my bed' has nothing to do with the field trip.
Fix: Remove that sentence. Optionally replace with a relevant detail: 'After the dome theater, our guide showed us a real meteorite that had crashed to Earth millions of years ago.'
solution.answer: Problem: 'I have a cat named Whiskers who likes to sleep on my bed' is off-topic. Remove it and replace with a detail about the museum visit.

items.prompt:
A student wrote this opinion piece. Identify TWO things that could be strengthened and write the improved version.

'I think parks are good. They are fun. Also parks are nice. Parks are important.'

steps: Problem 1: The reasons are too vague ('fun,' 'nice'). They need 'because' and specific details.
Problem 2: The closing sentence 'Parks are important' is weak — no explanation and no 'I' voice returning.

Improved: 'I think parks are important places in every neighborhood. Parks are fun because they give kids a safe place to run, climb, and play with friends after school. Also, parks are wonderful because they have trees and open spaces where families can relax and enjoy nature. That is why I believe every community should protect and care for its parks.'
solution.answer: Improved: 'I think parks are important places in every neighborhood. Parks are fun because they give kids a safe place to run, climb, and play with friends after school. Also, parks are wonderful because they have trees and open spaces where families can relax and enjoy nature. That is why I believe every community should protect and care for its parks.'

items.prompt:
Read this paragraph. Find the ONE sentence that is off-topic and should be removed.

'Butterflies are fascinating insects. They go through four stages of life: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, and butterfly. Pizza is my favorite food. Adult butterflies have wings covered in tiny, colorful scales.'
items.hint: Ask yourself: does every sentence connect to the main topic (butterflies)?

steps: Topic: butterflies. Check each sentence.
'Pizza is my favorite food' has nothing to do with butterflies.
That is the off-topic sentence to remove.
solution.answer: 'Pizza is my favorite food' is off-topic and should be removed.

items.prompt:
Revise this weak sentence by adding at least two specific details:

Weak: 'I helped my mom cook dinner.'
items.hint: Think about WHAT you made, HOW you helped, and HOW it felt.

steps: Add details: what dish? What specific task did you do? How did it turn out or how did you feel?
solution.answer: Sample: 'I helped my mom cook dinner by stirring the big pot of tomato soup and carefully slicing the bread while the kitchen filled with a warm, delicious smell.'

items.prompt:
Read the paragraph below. Which detail, if added, would MOST strengthen it? Choose and explain.

'I love playing soccer. I practice every day after school. It is my favorite sport.'

A) 'Soccer was invented in England.'
B) 'I practice dribbling cones and shooting on goal, and last week I finally scored my first goal in a real game.'
C) 'My shoes are blue and white.'
items.hint: Which option adds a personal, specific detail that connects to the writer's love of soccer?

steps: Option A is a general fact — not personal to the writer.
Option C is a minor detail about shoes that does not add meaning.
Option B gives a specific, exciting personal experience that directly supports 'I love playing soccer.'
solution.answer: B — it strengthens the paragraph by sharing a personal achievement that shows why the writer loves soccer.

items.prompt: A student's narrative ending is: 'We went home.' Revise it to give the story a proper sense of closure. The story is about a class trip to the aquarium.
items.hint: A strong ending includes how the character FELT and what they will remember.

steps: Replace the vague 'We went home' with a sentence that reflects on the experience.
solution.answer: Sample: 'On the bus ride back to school, everyone talked at once about their favorite moments, and I pressed my nose against the window and smiled, still thinking about the way the jellyfish had glowed blue in the dark.'

items.prompt:
Read this paragraph and identify TWO ways to strengthen it by revising. Then write your improved version.

'Rain is nice. It falls from clouds. Plants need rain. Rain is good.'
items.hint: What is vague? What is missing? How could each sentence be made more specific or interesting?

steps: Vague sentences: 'Rain is nice' and 'Rain is good' give no detail.
Missing: a sense of why rain matters and any specific details.
Improve by adding specific facts, details, or a definition.
solution.answer: Sample: 'Rain is one of nature's most important gifts to the living world. It falls from clouds when water droplets collect and grow heavy enough to fall back to Earth. Without rain, plants would dry up and die, and animals — including people — would not have fresh water to drink. Rain keeps our world green, clean, and full of life.'
